## Deviation from the original plan

The planned title for this week was *Gaussian Calculus & Markov Chains* (M2:
conditioning, marginalization, linear transformations, discrete-time Markov
chains). Mon Aug 17 instead followed the thread note 06 opened — sampling — from
Metropolis–Hastings through to GANs. Markov chains still appear, but as the
machinery behind MCMC rather than as a topic in their own right; the M2 material
on Gaussian calculus and noise accumulation moves forward.
:::

## In Class

**Mon Aug 17 — Prof. Uma.** Generative AI needs sampling from a distribution, and
that is a hard problem in general. When the target is known only up to its
normalising constant, Metropolis–Hastings applies: propose, accept with a ratio,
and the chain converges to a stationary distribution approximating the posterior.
Then the switch to deep generative modelling, starting with GANs — the Goodfellow
min-max formulation, the police-and-thief analogy, the derivation of the
objective, its equivalence at an optimal discriminator to minimising the
Jensen–Shannon divergence between the data distribution and the mixture of data
and generated distributions, and then the difficulties: vanishing gradients, slow
convergence, and instability.

**Lecture notes for this week:**

- [08 · Metropolis–Hastings: Sampling What You Cannot Normalise](../tutorials/18-metropolis-hastings.qmd)
  — the unnormalised-target problem, transition kernels and stationarity, detailed
  balance, the MH algorithm and its correctness proof, random-walk/independence/
  Gibbs/MALA as special cases, burn-in, ESS, step-size tuning and the $0.234$ rule,
  dimension scaling, and the structural reason MH cannot generate an image.
- [09 · Generative Adversarial Networks](../tutorials/19-generative-adversarial-networks.qmd)
  — implicit models, the counterfeiter analogy, the min-max objective, the optimal
  discriminator $D^{*} = p_{\text{data}}/(p_{\text{data}}+p_g)$, the
  $-\log 4 + 2\,\mathrm{JS}$ theorem, the saturating/non-saturating gradient
  computation, mode collapse, saddle-point non-convergence, and the MH ↔ GAN
  density-ratio correspondence.
